resources.string: Your weight swings by 1–2 kg from day to day, mostly water, salt, food and training. The trend smooths those swings out – each reading pulls it only a tenth of the way – so you see what really changes. Gaps are fine; weighing now and then is enough.
Weight trend from %1$s to %2$s, from %3$s to %4$s.
No weight logged yet. Tap + to start – weighing now and then is enough.
No measurements yet. Height and arm span once are enough for your ape index.
Arm span minus height. A positive value means your arms reach further than you are tall, which helps on long moves. It describes your build, not a training goal. Enter height and arm span once.
Enter height and arm span to see your ape index.
Progress through strength, not through the scale.

Shown is the best load per training day as a percentage of your body weight: for hangs body weight plus added weight, for block lifts the lifted weight, for weighted pull-ups the estimated maximum. Each set remembers the body weight of its day.
No data yet. The baseline test on the Today screen gives you a starting value.
Your history shows something that can point to too little energy. Eating enough is part of training – strength is built during recovery.

Too little energy over a longer time (RED-S) can affect performance, bones, hormones and mood. CruxCoach does not diagnose anything. If this sounds familiar – often tired, often ill, irregular periods, performance stalling – talk to a doctor or a sports nutrition professional.
Units and hiding numbers are in the training settings.
